name: ACC1c-1-the-salt-is-a-pepper
note: Every account then shares a zero salt: one rainbow table does the lot.

name: ACC1c-2-the-cost-is-a-token-gesture
note: A KDF nobody has to wait for is a KDF nobody has to wait for.

name: ACC1c-3-the-compare-short-circuits
why: Functionally identical, and the property it destroys - the time saying where the first differing byte was - is not one a node test can measure through a PBKDF2 derivation that dwarfs it. Held by reading rather than by timing, which is the honest place for it; the derivation in front of this compare is what actually makes the whole call constant-ish, and THAT is driven.

name: ACC1c-4-NFKC-is-skipped
note: A decomposed accent then locks its owner out of their own account, on a different keyboard.

name: ACC1c-5-a-parse-failure-verifies
note: An account with no password would then admit anybody.

name: ACC1c-6-an-unparseable-row-skips-the-derivation
old:
const got = await derive(pw, salt, iters, subtle);
  if (!parsed) return false;
new:
if (!parsed) return false;
  const got = await derive(pw, salt, iters, subtle);
note: Then 'this account has no password' is visibly faster than 'this password is wrong' - the username oracle, by the clock.

name: ACC1c-7-Q-is-folded-onto-zero-again
note: THE BUG ITS OWN PIN FOUND, put back: Q is in the alphabet, so a minted code carrying one canonicalises to a different string than the one that was hashed.

name: ACC1c-8-the-code-is-shorter-than-it-looks
note: Five characters is 25 bits, which is a weekend.

name: ACC1c-9-a-handle-nobody-holds-is-answered-early
old:
const ok = await verifyPassword(password, player?.password ?? null, { subtle });
  if (!player || !ok) return { error: 'bad-login' };
note: The username oracle, spelled out: a name nobody holds costs a lookup and a name somebody holds costs a derivation.

name: ACC1c-10-the-recovery-code-is-not-spent
old: UPDATE players SET password = ?, recovery_hash = ? WHERE id = ? AND recovery_hash = ?').bind(pw, rc, player.id, player.recovery_hash)
new: UPDATE players SET password = ? WHERE id = ? AND recovery_hash = ?').bind(pw, player.id, player.recovery_hash)
note: A code that still works after it has been used is a permanent skeleton key on a scrap of paper.

name: ACC1c-11-recovering-leaves-the-thief-signed-in
old:
await closeAllSessions({ db }, player.id);
  await clearRate({ db }, `recover:${lc}`);
note: The reason somebody is standing at recovery may be that another person has their password.

name: ACC1c-12-changing-a-password-needs-no-old-one
old: if (!await verifyPassword(oldPassword, player.password, { subtle })) return { error: 'bad-login' };
note: A borrowed phone could then lock its owner out of their own account.

name: ACC1c-13-a-taken-handle-is-checked-instead-of-enforced
old:
if (/UNIQUE|constraint/i.test(String(e?.message ?? e))) return { error: 'handle-taken' };
    throw e;
note: The UNIQUE index is the authority; without the catch, a race reads as a 500.

name: ACC1c-15-a-correct-login-does-not-forgive
note: Someone who mistyped twice and then got it right stays on a countdown.

name: ACC1c-16-registering-mints-a-new-account
old: WHERE id = ? AND handle IS NULL')
note: An upgrade in place is the property that keeps the friends and the saves.

name: ACC1c-17-login-and-recover-need-a-session
note: A player standing at a login form has no session - that is why they are standing there. (AUDIT-ACC F2 moved OPEN_ROUTES to service.js: the entrypoint may export only a handler, so the constants left index.js. Re-aimed at the new home and confirmed dead there.)

name: ACC1c-18-the-refusal-names-the-cause
why: The mutation appends a constant to every refusal rather than distinguishing the two cases, so the pin that compares the two bodies still sees them equal - it is not actually the defect it is named for. Kept as a record that the pin holds EQUALITY of the two refusals rather than their literal text, which is the property that matters and the one a real leak would break.
